chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is written in the Torah: O son of Adam! Remember Me when you are angered, I shall remember you during My anger, so I shall not eliminate you among those I eliminate.'
And whenever you are oppressed with an injustice, be pleased with My support for you, for My support for you is better than your support for yourself.
ai.seo_question: What does the Torah say about remembering God when angry and being patient with oppression?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the divine attribute of patience by linking human anger to God's wrath, instructing believers to invoke Allah during moments of rage to secure His mercy. It further encourages sabr (patience) in the face of oppression, asserting that divine retribution is superior to self-defense, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theological discussions on God's justice (Adl) and the virtue of enduring wrongs for His sake.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is Written in the Torah: “O son of Adam<sup>as</sup>! Remember me when you are angered, I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Remember you during My<sup>azwj</sup> Anger, so I<sup>azwj</sup> shall not Eliminate you among the ones I<sup>azwj</sup> do Eliminate;
and whenever you are oppressed with an injustice, so be pleased with My<sup>azwj</sup> Support for you, for My<sup>azwj</sup> Support for you is better than your support for yourself”’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Ishaq ibn ‘ Ammar who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘It is written in the Torah: “Remember Me when you are angry so I remember you when I am angry and will not efface you along with those whom I will blot out.
When injustice is done to you, accept My support; My support for you is better than your support for yourself.’”
